artifact.evidence_summary: The Literature Plugin searched PubMed with the query '"LINE1" AND "cancer" AND "cancer"', yielding 1289 candidates. It reviewed 8 citations and presented 5 previewed articles. The evidence includes: a 2020 paper on the chimeric L1-MET transcript in cancer (PMID 31918342); a 2017 review on transposable elements in cancer (PMID 28642606); a 2022 study on LINE1 splicing and T cell regulation (PMID 35039641); a 2025 paper showing LINE1-derived MET transcript inhibition induces apoptosis and oncoprotein knockdown in cancer cells (PMID 40291377); and a 2025 review on LINE-1 regulation and function (PMID 40382218). Additional citations cover LINE-1 retrotransposition in cancers, BMAL1-mediated repression, and TE-driven ecDNA in prostate cancer. No local library hits were found. The plugin provides adequate literature evidence for the mechanism question, though it lacks abstract summaries and deep curation.
caveats: PubMed query had redundant 'AND cancer', which may have slightly altered results

The paper on LINE1 splicing in T cells (PMID 35039641) may not directly address cancer mechanisms
Preprint (PMID 40832168) is included without qualification as non-peer-reviewed

preview_items.title: LINE-1 forms chimeric transcripts, such as L1-MET, which drive oncogenic pathways and are targetable.
preview_items.body: LINE-1 can fuse with the MET gene to produce a chimeric transcript (L1-MET) that is implicated in cancer. Inhibiting this transcript induces apoptosis and reduces oncoprotein levels, presenting a therapeutic opportunity.

preview_items.title: LINE-1 retrotransposition is derepressed in cancer, leading to insertional mutagenesis and genomic instability.
preview_items.body: LINE-1 elements are normally repressed, but in cancer, epigenetic dysregulation leads to increased retrotransposition, causing DNA damage, gene disruption, and chromosomal rearrangements that promote tumorigenesis.

preview_items.title: BMAL1 acts as a gatekeeper of LINE-1 repression, and its loss leads to LINE-1 activation, cellular senescence, and potentially cancer.
preview_items.body: BMAL1 protein moonlights to repress LINE-1 elements, maintaining genome stability and preventing senescence. Derepression of LINE-1 upon BMAL1 loss could contribute to aging and cancer.

preview_items.title: Epigenetic reprogramming of LINE-1 and other TEs promotes ecDNA-mediated metastasis.
preview_items.body: In prostate cancer, genetic and epigenetic changes activate transposable elements including LINE-1, contributing to the formation of extrachromosomal DNA (ecDNA) that drives metastatic progression.

preview_items.title: LINE-1 splicing produces transcript variants that regulate T cell function, which may influence cancer immune evasion.
preview_items.body: Non-canonical LINE-1 transcript variants are spliced and regulate T cell quiescence and exhaustion, suggesting a role in immune checkpoint biology that could affect cancer immunotherapy.
